analysis:
The change to docs/developer/test.md is documentation-only: the date bump at line 3 and a new 'Add-On Hold' test section at head lines ~767-790. The new section sits after line 766 in base, so the base units show only the pre-change context. The patch excerpt is truncated at 'The peer check is exercised only neg...', so the full added text was not visible. No source code, auth, crypto, attestation, or cache-storage controls changed in the supplied evidence, so I identified no security regression against the threat model.

The section describes tests for a new add-on hold feature: an AF_UNIX socket, flock, a peer policy, a drain/unload hold and a busy heartbeat field. It states the tests use a private temporary runtime directory, no credentials, and no live provider state. It also says the real peer policy refuses the test process.

The underlying add-on hold implementation is not in this batch. It may be new attack surface: a local IPC socket that can unload models and drain the provider (TB-003, local process vs provider; A-016, serving authorization; availability, T-057). Key points for review of the implementation:
- Socket permissions and peer-credential checks.
- Whether a hold can be asserted by an unprivileged local process.
- Whether hold or drain state interacts safely with App Attest connection control (TB-011, T-053) and reconnect.
- Lease expiry.

The doc claims these are tested, but documentation is not proof. No finding is raised because the implementation is not supplied. Recommend that source-code passes examine the AddonIPC server and peer policy, and that the threat model gain an entry for this local IPC boundary if it ships. The doc's isolation language is consistent with the existing 'must never stop an operator process' guidance.
